doc.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009

chapter: Coming to New Orleans and the clarinet tradition
title: Why the Albert system clarinet helps him
summary: The Albert fingering helps him get the Bechet and Simeon sounds. He composes in keys that suit it and did not own a good Albert clarinet until about 2000.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: From a finger standpoint some of the effects and the sounds that those players like Sidney Bechet and Omer Simeon — do you think it helps to have that instrument then?

And I’m constantly looking for things that are specific to this fingering system. You know I compose just to almost make a point that the New Orleans style has to be done on the Albert system. There’s things that I’ll put in. I’ll put things in certain keys so that they just don’t sound the same on a Boehm system clarinet. I didn’t actually have a good

Albert system clarinet until almost, until closer to 2000 I guess. So that was problematic as well. It helps me. It helps me feel like I’m more in there. Sort of like you can have a computer font that looks like an old typewriter ribbon, but it’s not really the same as typing on a typewriter.
